title: Python Fundamentals
description: Master the essential building blocks of Python programming. Learn variables, data types, operators, and basic input/output to start writing real Python code.
learningObjectives: Understand Python's basic data types (int, float, str, bool)
Write programs that accept user input and produce output

sections.content: Variables are like labeled boxes that store information in your computer's memory. In Python, creating a variable is as simple as giving it a name and assigning it a value using the equals sign (=).

# Creating variables
name = "Alice"
age = 25
height = 5.7
is_student = True

print(name)  # Output: Alice
print(age)   # Output: 25
💡 Python is dynamically typed - you don't need to declare the type of a variable. Python figures it out automatically!
Follow these rules when naming variables:

✅ Must start with a letter or underscore (_)
✅ Can contain letters, numbers, and underscores
✅ Case-sensitive (age and Age are different)
✅ Use snake_case for multi-word names
❌ Cannot use Python keywords (if, for, while, etc.)
❌ Cannot start with a number

# Good variable names
user_name = "Bob"
total_score = 100
_private_var = 42

# Bad variable names
2fast = 10  # Can't start with number
first-name = "John"  # Can't use hyphens
class = "Python 101"  # 'class' is a keyword
🎯 Pro tip: Use descriptive names! Instead of 'x' or 'n', use 'student_count' or 'user_age'. Your future self will thank you!
Variables can be reassigned new values at any time. The old value is replaced:

score = 0
print(score)  # Output: 0

score = 10
print(score)  # Output: 10

score = score + 5
print(score)  # Output: 15

examples.title: Creating Your First Variables
examples.code:
favorite_color = "blue"
lucky_number = 7
print(f"My favorite color is {favorite_color}")
print(f"My lucky number is {lucky_number}")
examples.output:
My favorite color is blue
My lucky number is 7
examples.explanation: This creates two variables: a string and an integer. We then use f-strings to print them in formatted messages.

examples.title: Variable Reassignment
examples.explanation: The temperature variable is first set to 72, then reassigned to 75. The new value replaces the old one.

examples.title: Multiple Assignments
examples.code:
x = y = z = 0
print(x, y, z)

a, b, c = 1, 2, 3
print(a, b, c)
examples.explanation: Python lets you assign the same value to multiple variables at once, or assign multiple values in one line.

exercises.question: Which of the following is a valid variable name in Python?
exercises.explanation: Variable names must start with a letter or underscore and can only contain letters, numbers, and underscores. Hyphens and spaces are not allowed, and you can't start with a number.

exercises.question: What will happen if you run: `class = "Python 101"`?
options: The variable will be named 'Class' instead
It will print an error message
exercises.explanation: 'class' is a reserved keyword in Python used for defining classes. You cannot use keywords as variable names.

exercises.question: What will be printed?
exercises.explanation: x starts at 5, then we add 3 to it and reassign the result (8) back to x.

exercises.question: Create two variables `a = 10` and `b = 20`. Then swap their values so that a becomes 20 and b becomes 10. Print both variables.
exercises.starterCode:
a = 10
b = 20

# Swap the values here


print(a)
print(b)
exercises.solution:
a = 10
b = 20

# Swap the values here
a, b = b, a

print(a)
print(b)
hints: Python allows multiple assignments in one line
You can do: a, b = b, a
No need for a temporary variable in Python!
